result.keywords: A fictional study presenting a hybrid sensing framework for gesture interaction in soft robotic systems. The work combines wearable pressure sensing and contactless radar-style sensing to improve recognition of hand and wrist motions in modular human-centric robots. A hierarchical classifier is used to fuse heterogeneous data streams with different sampling characteristics and signal formats, enabling robust gesture interpretation across changing robot configurations. Experiments are described on a moderate-sized participant dataset, and the hybrid approach is reported to outperform either sensing mode alone. The article also discusses modular actuation, safe human-robot interaction, adaptive locomotion, and potential applications in rehabilitation and assistive technologies.
result.title: Adaptive Hybrid Soft Sensing for Modular Gesture Interaction in Human-Centric Robotics
